newsitem.title: USA: Novartis settlement still needs court approval.
newsitem.headline: Novartis settlement still needs court approval.

text.p: Massachusetts Attorney General Scott Harshbarger said in a statement on Monday that a settlement reached by a number of states with a Novartis AG unit on contact lens pricing still must be approved by a federal judge in Jacksonville, Fla..

In class action and state lawsuits, Harshbarger's office and others alleged that CIBA Vision, along with Johnson & Johnson's Vistakon, Bausch & Lomb Inc, the American Optometric Association and other defendants conspired not to sell replacement contact lens directly to retailers like pharmacies and mail-order companies.
The settlement does not end the lawsuits pending against Vistakon, Bausch & Lomb, eight optometric associations and 11 optometrists.

CIBA has changed its distribution policy to make its contact lens available through mail-order, pharmacies and other ways, and, according to the settlement, the policy must be in place for five years.
Other manufacturers have not changed their policies, the Mass. Attorney General's office said.
